newItems.title: Unpacking Open Source Artificial Intelligence: Toward a Framework for Openness in Foundation Models
newItems.tldr: A framework for analyzing openness across the AI stack is proposed, reviewing prior approaches and highlighting the diverse motivations for pursuing openness, showing how these map onto different forms of openness at both the model and system levels.
newItems.abstract: There has been a robust debate about the benefits and risks of “open sourcing” foundation models. Yet much of the discourse has lacked specificity, either remaining overly abstract or focusing narrowly on a limited set of technical components. This is partly because defining open source for foundation models is challenging, given their significant differences from traditional software development. To inform a more practical and nuanced discussion of openness in AI systems, including foundation models, we propose a framework for analyzing openness across the AI stack. newItems.title: RepFusion: Leveraging Multimodal Priors for Denoising in Representation Space
newItems.tldr: It is demonstrated that MLLMs provide strong priors for denoising visual representations and that, by conditioning on evolving noisy representations, test-time compute can be productively spent on repeated MLLM conditioning in modern T2I systems.
newItems.abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are widely used in text-to-image (T2I) systems, but they are typically limited to text encoding, while denoising is handled by newly trained generative backbones. The emergence of representation autoencoders (RAEs) shifts the generation target toward semantically structured visual representations, creating a latent space that is more compatible with pretrained LLM priors. newItems.title: Plan, Watch, Recover: A Benchmark and Architectures for Proactive Procedural Assistance
newItems.tldr: The trained Llama-4 system substantially improves objective intervention quality over strong proprietary baselines and open-weight baselines across all six datasets, and Oracle-plan experiments further show that, when plan quality is controlled, the trained duplex model produces high-quality guidance and large gains on Out-of-Plan recovery.
newItems.abstract: We envision a proactive multi-modal assistant system which gives users real-time step-by-step guidance on a procedural task, autonomously deciding \textit{when} to interrupt, and \textit{how} to coach. However, progress is limited by the absence of large-scale, cross-domain benchmarks that reflect realistic conditions, particularly the common case in which users deviate from the expected step sequence. newItems.title: Formalizing Mathematics at Scale
newItems.abstract: We present AutoformBot, a multi-agent system for building an Autoformalized Textbook Library At Scale (Atlas) in Lean 4. AutoformBot orchestrates thousands of LLM agents, equipped with formal verification tools, dependency-aware task scheduling, and collaborative version control, to translate informal textbook prose into machine-checked definitions and proofs. We apply our methods to a corpus of 26 open-access textbooks spanning analysis, algebra, topology, combinatorics, and probability, producing Atlas: a verified library of over 45,000 Lean 4 declarations and 500 thousand lines of code. newItems.title: Formalization of De Giorgi--Nash--Moser Theory in Lean
newItems.abstract: We present a formalization in Lean of the core interior De Giorgi--Nash--Moser theory for uniformly elliptic divergence-form equations with bounded measurable coefficients. The formalized results include local boundedness of weak subsolutions, the weak Harnack inequality for positive weak supersolutions, Moser's Harnack inequality for positive weak solutions, and interior H\"older regularity. This is, to our knowledge, the first machine-checked formalization of a major theorem in modern PDE theory. newItems.title: Repurposing Geometric Foundation Models for Multi-view Diffusion
newItems.tldr: This paper proposes Geometric Latent Diffusion (GLD), a framework that repurposes the geometrically consistent feature space of geometric foundation models as the latent space for multi-view diffusion, and shows that these features not only support high-fidelity RGB reconstruction but also encode strong cross-view geometric correspondences, providing a well-suited latent space for NVS.

newItems.title: Reward Prediction with Factorized World States
newItems.tldr: This paper investigates whether well-defined world state representations alone can enable accurate reward prediction across domains, and shows promising zero-shot results against both VLWM-critic and LLM-as-a-Judge reward models.

newItems.title: What matters for Representation Alignment: Global Information or Spatial Structure?
newItems.tldr: Surprisingly, the simple method, termed iREPA, consistently improves convergence speed of REPA, across a diverse set of vision encoders, model sizes, and training variants (such as REPA, REPA-E, Meanflow, JiT etc).

newItems.title: DiffusionGuard: A Robust Defense Against Malicious Diffusion-based Image Editing
newItems.tldr: This work proposes DiffusionGuard, a robust and effective defense method against unauthorized edits by diffusion-based image editing models, even in challenging setups, and introduces a novel objective that generates adversarial noise targeting the early stage of the diffusion process.

newItems.title: REPA-E: Unlocking VAE for End-to-End Tuning with Latent Diffusion Transformers
newItems.venue: IEEE International Conference on Computer Vision
newItems.tldr: It is shown that while diffusion loss is ineffective, end-to-end training can be unlocked through the representation-alignment (REPA) loss - allowing both VAE and diffusion model to be jointly tuned during the training process.

newItems.title: International AI Safety Report
newItems.abstract: The first International AI Safety Report comprehensively synthesizes the current evidence on the capabilities, risks, and safety of advanced AI systems. The report was mandated by the nations attending the AI Safety Summit in Bletchley, UK. Thirty nations, the UN, the OECD, and the EU each nominated a representative to the report's Expert Advisory Panel. A total of 100 AI experts contributed, representing diverse perspectives and disciplines. Led by the report's Chair, these independent experts collectively had full discretion over the report's content.

newItems.title: International Scientific Report on the Safety of Advanced AI (Interim Report)
newItems.tldr: The report synthesises the scientific understanding of general-purpose AI -- AI that can perform a wide variety of tasks -- with a focus on understanding and managing its risks.
newItems.abstract: This is the interim publication of the first International Scientific Report on the Safety of Advanced AI. The report synthesises the scientific understanding of general-purpose AI -- AI that can perform a wide variety of tasks -- with a focus on understanding and managing its risks. A diverse group of 75 AI experts contributed to this report, including an international Expert Advisory Panel nominated by 30 countries, the EU, and the UN. Led by the Chair, these independent experts collectively had full discretion over the report's content. The final report is available at arXiv:2501.17805

headline: Min Lin's Video Codec Push Points to a Quiet but Telling Infrastructure Bet
stateOfPlay: This was a week of background signals rather than announcements. We had no big news this week or hiring added (though more coming next week!). A cluster of research publications surfaced across AMI's team, though most predated this window. And there was a small but pointed burst of engineering activity from Min Lin on video decoding infrastructure.

threads.title: Min Lin is working on video infrastructure
threads.narrative:
The most concrete signal this week comes not from a paper but from a pull request. Min Lin opened PR #1629 against meta-pytorch/torchcodec and created a personal branch called agent/vfr-timestamp-batches-review . TorchCodec is Meta's library for decoding video into tensors; variable-frame-rate (VFR) timestamp handling is precisely the kind of low-level plumbing that matters when you are training models on heterogeneous real-world video at scale.

The branch name's 'agent' prefix is suggestive rather than conclusive, but it points toward one plausible interpretation: someone at AMI is investing in reliable, batched video decoding as a dependency for something downstream — whether that is a world-model training pipeline, an agentic system that must process egocentric video, or both. The fact that Lin is working against the upstream Meta repo, not a private fork, suggests this is infrastructure intended to be shared or contributed back, which in turn implies it is foundational rather than product-specific. Seven activity events from Brian Li in the same window, with no associated notable items, suggest parallel engineering work we cannot yet characterize.

threads.title: Saining Xie's generative vision work is maturing into a coherent research program
threads.narrative:
Several publications attributed to Saining Xie surfaced in this window's count as we continued to expand the backend for capturing the team's research. This research describes a sustained, coherent program in generative visual representations. RepFusion (arXiv, June 2026) proposes repurposing multimodal LLMs as denoisers in representation space. This is essentially arguing that the semantic structure of MLLM priors can be redirected toward image generation via representation autoencoders. This builds directly on REPA-E (ICCV 2025, 195 citations), which showed that end-to-end VAE-and-diffusion training becomes tractable only when representation alignment is introduced as a training signal. The iREPA work (arXiv, December 2025, 63 citations) then refined the question further, finding that spatial structure in the target representation matters as much as global semantic quality.

The arc is clear: Xie's group is systematically exploring what makes a latent space well-suited for generation, and the answer they are converging on is geometric and semantic structure — not raw pixel fidelity. The Geometric Latent Diffusion paper (arXiv, March 2026) extends this to multi-view synthesis, using geometric foundation models to supply a cross-view-consistent latent space. For AMI, whose stated agenda includes world models, this line of work is directly relevant: learning to generate geometrically consistent views of a scene is a prerequisite for building internal models of three-dimensional space.

threads.title: Julia Kempe's formal mathematics work is an outlier. Or is it?
threads.narrative:
Julia Kempe appears this week with two papers on the machine formalization of mathematics in Lean 4. AutoformBot (arXiv, May 2026, 4 citations) describes a multi-agent system that translated 26 open-access textbooks into over 45,000 machine-verified Lean declarations. The De Giorgi–Nash–Moser formalization (April 2026, 8 citations) claims to be the first machine-checked proof of a major modern PDE theorem. Neither paper is about neural networks in the conventional sense.

This is worth flagging precisely because it sits so far from AMI's publicly stated focus on world models and embodied intelligence. Kempe's investment here suggests AMI is at least adjacent to, if not actively interested in, the question of whether LLM-assisted formal verification can serve as a scalable source of ground-truth mathematical reasoning data — a line of thinking that connects to the broader agenda around AI that can reason reliably. It could also simply reflect Kempe's independent research interests maintained alongside AMI work. Either way, the presence of frontier formal-methods work in AMI's publication orbit is worth tracking.

signals.text: LeCun's Communications of the ACM piece on open-source AI proposes a framework for analyzing 'openness' across the full AI stack — a policy-facing intervention, not a technical one, and a reminder that AMI's co-founder is still actively shaping the normative debate around open models.

Pascale Fung's 'Plan, Watch, Recover' benchmark (arXiv, June 2026) introduces EgoProactive, an egocentric dataset for proactive procedural assistance, and trains a Llama-4-based system that outperforms proprietary baselines on out-of-plan recovery — a concrete step toward real-time wearable assistants.

whatToWatch: The agent/vfr-timestamp-batches-review branch is the one to follow: if Min Lin's torchcodec work merges upstream and is followed by new AMI repos or papers referencing video-based training, it will confirm that scalable video decoding is a live infrastructure dependency — most likely for a world-model or agentic training pipeline. Separately, watch whether Saining Xie's geometric latent diffusion line produces a system-level demonstration; the theoretical scaffolding is now substantial enough that an application paper feels close.
